subject: physics
question_text: If a bomb at rest explodes into two pieces, the pieces must travel in opposite directions. Explain.

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 5 VERY SHORT ANSWER. The 1+1 mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for this question, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Before the blast
lines: The bomb is at rest, so the total
momentum before the explosion is zero.
Momentum is conserved, so after it:
steps.margin_note: Start from zero. Everything in this answer follows from that one word.
steps.why: The explosion is internal. It can hand momentum from one piece to the other, but it cannot create any for the pair.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to say the initial momentum is zero, then having nothing to conclude from.

recall.must_convey: That the bomb is at rest so the total momentum is zero, and it stays zero.
accept: bomb at rest so momentum zero
momentum is conserved and it was zero
modata bomb rest lo undi momentum zero
reject: the pieces move in opposite directions

steps.memory_tip: Momentum before = 0, and the explosion is internal, so momentum after = 0 too.

steps.label: Why opposite
lines: The two momenta are equal in size and
opposite in sign, so the pieces must
steps.margin_note: The minus sign IS the answer. Write it, then say what it means.
steps.why: Two vectors can add to zero only if they point opposite ways. The masses need not be equal — the momenta must be.
common_mistakes: Claiming the two pieces have equal SPEEDS. Only their momenta match.

recall.must_convey: That the two momenta are equal and opposite, so the pieces travel in opposite directions.
accept: so they move in opposite directions

steps.memory_tip: Two momenta adding to zero must point opposite ways: m₁v₁ = −m₂v₂.

insider_note: The second mark is the direction sentence, not the equation. An answer that stops at m₁v₁ = −m₂v₂ has not yet said "opposite directions".
